rows.what_the_ink_shows: After ‘par l’Idéal’, the manuscript has a calligraphic J-shaped character followed immediately at its upper right by a compact p-shaped stroke (crops/46_scan011_L899_ideal.png). The same two-part group is repeated to the right of the equals sign in ‘l’hyp. s’écrit J = J^p’ (crops/46_scan011_L899_equality.png). No square brackets enclosing p are visible at either occurrence. The context crop includes the preceding definition of the ideal J and the ensuing conclusion that the immersion is open. The supplied TeX’s two doubt-marked readings of J^p match this visible notation, and their existing doubt marks are retained.
rows.note: Keep the two existing \unsure{\mathcal J^p} readings. The source uses the unbracketed p notation at both loci; the supplied proposed correction refines its mathematical meaning. As supplied in L899, the base change is defined by the Frobenius power J^[p], the ideal generated by p-th powers, so the intended equality is J = J^[p]; the row further says that the idempotence conclusion J = J^2 follows either way. This is recorded as the row’s mathematical qualification, not as an independently checked proof or as bracket strokes present in the manuscript. No extra equation or bracket notation is inserted into the diplomatic text.

check_event.type: used and rechecked in this run
check_event.outcome: Inspected the whole scan and separately viewed tight enlarged, contrast-raised crops of the ideal notation and its repetition in the equality, plus a context crop. Confirmed repeated unbracketed J/p-shaped notation and absence of visible square brackets. Classified L899 as b, retaining the original doubt-marked transcription without an edit. No OCR or mathematical proof checking was used.
